map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.

legend.definition: The key explaining the symbols on a map.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

compass-rose.definition: A symbol on a map showing directions such as north, south, east, and west.
compass-rose.exampleUsage: The compass rose shows which way is north.

grid.definition: A pattern of regularly spaced horizontal and vertical lines.

coordinates.definition: Numbers that identify a location on a map or grid.

latitude.definition: A location's angular distance north or south of the equator.

longitude.definition: The angular distance between a point on any meridian and the prime meridian at Greenwich.

contour.definition: A line drawn on a map connecting points of equal height.

boundary.definition: The line or plane indicating the limit or extent of something.

gps.definition: A satellite-based system used to find a location.

compass.exampleUsage: The compass was used during the activity.

satellite.definition: A machine sent into space to collect information and send it back.
satellite.exampleUsage: The satellite was used during the activity.

radar.definition: A system that uses radio waves to detect objects or weather.

binoculars.definition: An instrument used for seeing distant objects more clearly.
binoculars.exampleUsage: The binoculars was used during the activity.

telescope.definition: An instrument that makes distant objects appear closer.

altimeter.definition: An instrument that measures the height above ground.
altimeter.exampleUsage: The altimeter was used during the activity.

speedometer.definition: A meter fixed to a vehicle that measures and displays its speed.

odometer.definition: A meter that shows mileage traversed.

sextant.definition: A navigation instrument that measures the angle between two visible objects.

route.definition: A planned way from one place to another.

path.definition: A line or route along which something travels or moves.

trail.definition: A path through a natural area for walking.

shortcut.definition: A route shorter than the usual one.

detour.definition: A roundabout road (especially one that is used temporarily while a main route is blocked).

destination.definition: The place designated as the end (as of a race or journey).

origin.definition: The place where something begins, where it springs into being.
origin.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Origin" in an educational description.

waypoint.definition: A specified location used as a reference point along a route.
waypoint.exampleUsage: The route includes a waypoint near the bridge.

milestone.definition: Stone post at side of a road to show distances.

checkpoint.definition: A place (as at a frontier) where travellers are stopped for inspection and clearance.

navigation-app.definition: A software application that provides maps, routes, directions, or location information.
navigation-app.exampleUsage: The navigation app displayed the walking route.

pin.definition: A number you choose and use to gain access to various accounts.

search.definition: To look for information in a program or online.

directions.definition: Instructions explaining how to reach a place.

estimated-time.definition: An approximate amount of time expected for an event, journey, or task.
estimated-time.exampleUsage: The app showed an estimated travel time of twenty minutes.

reroute.definition: To change the route taken to a destination.

satellite-view.definition: A map display based mainly on imagery captured from satellites or aircraft.
satellite-view.exampleUsage: Satellite view showed the shape of the coastline.

street-view.definition: A map feature that displays ground-level photographs of streets and public places.
street-view.exampleUsage: Street view helped identify the building entrance.

share-location.definition: To send another person digital information showing a current or chosen location.
share-location.exampleUsage: She shared the meeting location with her parent.
